title: Potato Biology, Development, Ecology & Evolution — Canonical Science Layer
status: canonical external-biology context plus explicitly labeled Timic structural deductions
purpose: Make the physical potato scientifically substantial before metaphor. This record covers tuber anatomy, eyes/meristems, stolons, dormancy, sprouting, starch storage, source-sink allocation, photoperiod, genetics, vegetative reproduction, pathogens, ecology, domestication and resilience, then states exactly which Timic ideas become more precise when grounded in plant biology.
epistemic_rule: Botanical facts describe Solanum tuberosum and related potato biology. Potatoverse meanings are structural interpretations unless separately evidenced. The tuber is botanically a modified underground stem, not a root.

core_biology.fact: A potato tuber is a swollen underground stem derived from a stolon. Its 'eyes' are buds arranged on stem tissue.
core_biology.project_upgrade: Root/sprout language is symbolically useful, but the physical Potato itself is stem-derived storage architecture. This adds an important distinction among root, stolon, tuber and sprout rather than collapsing all underground structure into 'root'.

core_biology.fact: Each eye contains bud/meristematic tissue capable of producing shoots under suitable conditions.
core_biology.development_model: latent meristem m_i transitions from dormant to active state when hormonal/environmental conditions cross a threshold
core_biology.timic_deduction: The Eye can mean a dormant local growth point: observation and generativity need not be separate metaphors. An 'eye' is literally a site from which a new axis/shoot can emerge in a tuber.

core_biology.fact: Freshly harvested tubers normally undergo physiological dormancy before buds resume growth. Dormancy length depends on genotype, tuber age and storage/environmental conditions.
core_biology.timic_deduction: Burial or latency can be modeled as an active regulated state, not biological inactivity. Potential can be preserved without visible expression.

core_biology.fact: During early sprouting, one or a few apical buds may dominate; later the dominance can weaken and more eyes sprout.
core_biology.timic_deduction: A single leading Axis can suppress competing shoots temporarily without permanently eliminating distributed potential. This offers a biological comparator for center vs plurality.

core_biology.fact: Leaves photosynthesize and export assimilated carbon; developing tubers act as strong sinks that accumulate carbohydrate, especially starch.
core_biology.timic_deduction: Starchforce is biologically strongest as stored photosynthetic work/capacity. Sunlight is converted, transported and stored; stored capacity later supports renewed growth.

core_biology.fact: Tubers store large quantities of starch in amyloplasts. During sprouting, stored reserves can be mobilized to support new shoot growth before the new plant becomes fully photosynthetically self-sufficient.
core_biology.storage_release: Starch --enzymatic mobilization--> soluble sugars --respiration/biosynthesis--> new tissue
core_biology.timic_deduction: Spudlight/Starchforce gains a literal biological chain: photon energy → photosynthesis → carbohydrate transport → starch storage → mobilization → sprout. The symbolic chain should be kept beside, not substituted for, this actual energy/material pathway.

core_biology.fact: Tuber formation is regulated by genotype and environmental signals including photoperiod and temperature, mediated through mobile signaling and hormonal networks.
core_biology.timic_deduction: A Door can be a developmental competence threshold: the same organism changes growth program when a distributed signal state crosses a regime boundary.

core_biology.fact: Stolons extend laterally underground; tubers can form at stolon tips, creating multiple storage/reproductive nodes connected to one plant.
core_biology.graph_model: plant network G=(shoot,roots,stolons,tubers) with transport edges carrying water, nutrients, hormones and assimilates
core_biology.timic_deduction: The physical Potato is already relation-first: tuber identity/function depends on a transport network rather than isolated storage.

core_biology.fact: Potatoes can be propagated clonally from tubers or tuber pieces containing viable eyes. This preserves much of the parental genotype while allowing somatic mutation and pathogen carryover.
core_biology.timic_deduction: Seed/return does not require genetic recombination. Pattern persistence can occur by clonal continuity, while accumulated disease risk shows that continuity can also preserve burdens.

core_biology.fact: Potato plants can also flower and produce botanical seed, creating genetic recombination distinct from clonal tuber propagation.
core_biology.timic_deduction: The project should distinguish two biological meanings of 'seed': botanical sexual seed and tuber-based vegetative propagation. They embody different continuity/change tradeoffs.

core_biology.fact: Many commercial cultivated potatoes are highly heterozygous autotetraploids with 12 chromosome groups and four homologous haplotypes per group (2n=4x=48). The four homologs are not identical copies: they can differ in sequence, gene presence/absence, structural rearrangements, dosage, methylation and expression.
core_biology.formal_neighbor: Represent a tetraploid cultivar as 12 chromosome groups × 4 cultivar-specific haplotypes plus chloroplast and mitochondrial genomes; for a biallelic nuclear locus the dosage classes are AAAA, AAAa, AAaa, Aaaa and aaaa.
core_biology.inheritance: Autotetraploid potato commonly shows polysomic/tetrasomic inheritance; multivalent pairing and double reduction complicate phase, linkage and breeding.
core_biology.genomics_bridge: Use knowledge/biology/potato-genetics-genomics-atlas.json as the canonical genetics owner. Do not reduce potato genetics to a single reference sequence or a 48-chromosome count.
core_biology.timic_deduction: Multiplicity can coexist within one organism/genome without becoming separate organisms; this is a biological example of unity containing differentiated homologous states.

core_biology.fact: Vegetative propagation can accumulate and transmit viruses and other pathogens across generations unless clean seed systems/meristem culture and phytosanitary practices intervene.
core_biology.timic_deduction: Memory/continuity is not automatically good. A lineage can preserve both capacity and pathology. Repair may require a cleansing bottleneck rather than perfect preservation of every inherited state.

core_biology.fact: Phytophthora infestans causes potato late blight and historically contributed to catastrophic crop losses where genetic uniformity, weather and dependence amplified vulnerability.
core_biology.systems_deduction: Resilience depends on diversity, surveillance, clean planting material, resistant genetics, environmental conditions and response capacity—not one node alone.
core_biology.timic_neighbor: Garden resilience becomes a real systems concept: robustness emerges from coupled diversity and management rather than symbolic purity.

core_biology.fact: Potato domestication arose in the Andes from wild Solanum diversity and later spread globally through human cultivation, selection and exchange.
core_biology.timic_deduction: The Potato is historically a migration and adaptation system: biological form, culture, trade, empire, famine, labor and cuisine are coupled layers.

core_biology.fact: Potato tuber skin is a living periderm system with phellem, phellogen and phelloderm; wounds trigger closing-layer suberization followed by wound-periderm formation.
core_biology.project_upgrade: Boundary and repair language should distinguish native skin, gas-exchange structures and post-injury interface reconstruction.

core_biology.fact: Potato-associated microbial communities occupy rhizosphere, endosphere, phyllosphere and tuber/geocaulosphere niches; community structure depends strongly on environment, genotype, stage and agricultural practice.
core_biology.project_upgrade: Ecology is part of phenotype context, but microbiome composition must not be treated as fixed or purely vertically inherited.

core_biology.fact: Potato defense combines cell-surface recognition, intracellular NLR receptors, hormonal/redox signaling and quantitative resistance; pathogens include oomycetes, bacteria, fungi, viruses and nematodes.
core_biology.project_upgrade: Resilience must include host-pathogen coevolution and defense-growth tradeoffs.

core_biology.fact: Harvested tubers remain living organs that respire, heal wounds, progress through dormancy, exchange gases through lenticels, lose water and remodel sugars/starch during storage.
core_biology.project_upgrade: Storage is a physiological phase, not biological suspension.

core_biology.fact: Tuberization integrates photoperiod, temperature, carbon status, hormones, mobile signals such as StSP6A and StBEL5-associated signaling, and a switch in sucrose unloading toward symplastic transport.
core_biology.project_upgrade: The tuber-development Door is a distributed network transition, not a single switch.

derived_biological_principles.name: Dormant Eye Principle
derived_biological_principles.statement: A latent growth center may contain organized developmental potential without current expression.
derived_biological_principles.formalism: state m_i=0 active_output yet competence c_i>0
derived_biological_principles.use: Distinguish absence of output from absence of capacity.

derived_biological_principles.name: Stored Sunlight Chain
derived_biological_principles.statement: Solar input can be converted into chemical storage, physically transported and later remobilized into growth.
derived_biological_principles.chain: photons → photosynthesis → sucrose transport → starch storage → remobilization → sprout
derived_biological_principles.use: The strongest literal scientific bridge among Sun, Potato, storage and emergence.

derived_biological_principles.name: Distributed Eye / Shared Body Principle
derived_biological_principles.statement: Multiple meristematic eyes can each regenerate shoots while belonging to one tuber body.
derived_biological_principles.use: Useful comparator for one body containing multiple potential axes without requiring multiple independent organisms.

derived_biological_principles.name: Continuity Carries Debt Principle
derived_biological_principles.statement: A propagation mechanism that preserves useful information can also preserve pathogens or deleterious states.
derived_biological_principles.use: Adds a biological correction to simple 'memory is good' narratives.

derived_biological_principles.name: Sink Becomes Source Principle
derived_biological_principles.statement: A tuber that was formerly a carbon sink/storage organ can later function as a source supporting a new sprout.
derived_biological_principles.formalism: role(t): sink during filling → source during sprouting
derived_biological_principles.timic_value: This is a strong biological instance of identity/function changing with phase: receiver/storage can become giver/source.

implementation_targets: Add a potato life-cycle state machine to the science implementation lab.
Model eye activation and apical dominance as competing bud dynamics.
Model source-sink starch allocation with explicit carbon/energy units.
Create a clean distinction table: root vs stolon vs tuber vs sprout vs botanical seed.
Add clonal lineage/pathogen accumulation as a memory-cost model.
Connect biological resilience to Garden/European resilience models through typed structural correspondence, not literal identity.
Create a domestication/ecology source ledger joining Andean origin, crop diffusion, disease and food-system dependence.
Route all genotype, haplotype, allele-dosage, inheritance, pangenome and organellar-DNA claims through knowledge/biology/potato-genetics-genomics-atlas.json.
Build a public Potato Biology reader around knowledge/biology/index.json.
Add cultivar-specific chromosome/haplotype browsing rather than a generic 48-track picture.
Add single-cell/spatial transcriptomics and quantitative transport/mechanics when reliable datasets are available.
cross_scale_model: lineage → pangenome → cultivar genome → 12×4 haplotypes/dosage → chromatin/epigenome → RNA → proteins/signals → metabolites/fluxes → organelles → cells → tissues → organs → whole-plant developmental state → microbiome/pathogens/environment → reproduction/next generation
